summary: The current repository still presents a coherent, near-complete customer delivery surface for the desktop product, backed by fresh GO release evidence and passing live contract checks. The remaining meaningful customer-facing gap is a likely Evaluation panel endpoint drift for the novel quality check action, plus a process-level gap in preserving the full sign-off evidence pack inside the repo.

final_assessment.judgment: 核心桌面交付面已经完整到可交付客户的程度，但还不是零瑕疵的 handoff。主流程、文档口径、打包线索、关键 UI/API 契约和工作流门禁都闭合且现时验证通过；不过 Evaluation 面板里仍有一个很可能真实可见的旧接口调用缺口，另外正式签收要求保留的 XML/authority 工件没有在当前仓库快照内一起留存。

ux_completeness_findings.title: Writer-first shell feels materially complete
ux_completeness_findings.detail: The desktop surface is composed as a product shell rather than a dev scaffold, with empty-state guidance, runtime status, checkpoint controls, error boundary, editor export actions, and modular right-side tool panels.

ux_completeness_findings.title: UI and backend are aligned for the core promised customer journeys
ux_completeness_findings.detail: Chat, knowledge, settings/runtime diagnostics, wiki promotion, workflow routing/execution, and MCP admin services all map to real backend routes and now have matching targeted tests.

ux_completeness_findings.title: Workflow control includes visible and tested guardrails
ux_completeness_findings.detail: Destructive workflow execution requires a confirmation token in backend risk-gate logic, and integration tests verify the waiting-confirmation path before execution proceeds.

ux_completeness_findings.title: No dedicated onboarding wizard, but first-run guidance is adequate
ux_completeness_findings.detail: There is no multi-step onboarding flow. Instead, the first-run experience relies on the chat empty state, quick mode buttons, workspace chips, runtime status, and settings access. This is acceptable for a desktop tool aimed at writer/operators, but not premium-polish onboarding.

ux_completeness_findings.title: Novel quality check action likely points at a dead endpoint
ux_completeness_findings.detail: This is an inference from source alignment: the Evaluation panel exposes a visible quality-check action via useEvaluationQualityCheck -> novelQualityCheck(), but the frontend posts to /api/novel/quality-check while the gateway route registry exposes /writing/quality. Unless another compatibility server provides the old path at runtime, the button is likely broken.

ux_completeness_findings.title: Formal proof pack is incomplete inside the checkout
ux_completeness_findings.detail: The current repo includes the fresh release summary and release-readiness artifact, but not the standalone authority-alignment JSON or the XML reports listed by SIGN_OFF.md as artifacts to keep. This is a handoff-traceability gap rather than a core product-surface blocker.

customer_handoff_risks.risk: Visible Evaluation panel feature may fail at runtime
customer_handoff_risks.why: Only one visible sub-flow appears drifted; the main release contract and core flows remain intact.

customer_handoff_risks.risk: Proof bundle for external sign-off is not fully preserved in-repo
customer_handoff_risks.why: A customer handoff can still proceed with the fresh summary plus rerunnable gates, but formal auditability is weaker unless CI/local artifacts are exported together with the build.

questions_for_analysis: Is the Evaluation panel novel-quality-check action part of the customer-promised scope for this delivery, or can it be downgraded to a known caveat?
Will the final handoff package include the CI-generated XML and authority artifacts listed in SIGN_OFF.md, or should the repo-local proof set be refreshed and exported first?
